# Auto Ontology Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need a context layer that tells them where data lives, what it means, whether to use it, how to use it, where it came from, and what is similar. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that layer from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own. It enables developers to: - Discover: generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - Ground: give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage; return provenance with every answer. - Expose: serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. Learn: fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with every question. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to the [ontology SQL evaluation repository](https://github.com/NVIDIA/ontology-sql-eval/). > **Licensing & contributions.** Auto Ontology is distributed under the > [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). Third-party open-source components > bundled, linked, or otherwise used by this project are listed in > [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). **This project > is currently not accepting external contributions.**

## Key Features - **Natural-language querying** of structured data — questions are translated to SQL and executed against connected databases, powered by NVIDIA NIM. - **Semantic catalog / ontology layer** over relational sources, stored in Postgres alongside the catalog it describes. - **Authentication & RBAC** —using [Better Auth](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth). - **Web UI** for chat, analysis, data catalog, analytics, and settings. - **Flexible deployment** — Helm chart for Kubernetes or Docker Compose for a local stack. ## Software Components | Component | Technology | Role | Default port | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------ | | Frontend | Next.js 16 (React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4), Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Chat / NL-to-SQL, catalog, datasource APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion worker | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingests tabular data and writes embeddings | 3002 | | Postgres + pgvector | Relational Database | App metadata, the catalog and ontology, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Secure storage of connection credentials | — | ### NVIDIA NIM Auto Ontology uses NVIDIA NIM endpoints for inference — either the hosted [NVIDIA API catalog](https://build.nvidia.com) (`integrate.api.nvidia.com`) or self-hosted NIMs. The defaults in `.env.example` are: - **LLM:** `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` - **Embeddings:** `nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b` - **Reranking:** `nvidia/llama-nemotron-rerank-vl-1b-v2` The endpoints and models are configured via the `DEFAULT_MODELS_ENDPOINT`, `DEFAULT_MODELS_MODEL`, `EMBED_ENDPOINT`, and `EMBED_MODEL` environment variables and require a `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. #### Model triplets Each model role is configured by a **triplet** of environment variables — `_ENDPOINT` (URL), `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`: | Prefix | Role | | ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `DEFAULT_MODELS` | Shared default; every field below falls back to it. | | `REASONING` | Main chat / NL-to-SQL model. | | `NON_REASONING` | Lighter model used for entity extraction. | | `EMBED` | Text-embedding model (must match between ingest and query). | | `RERANK` | Reranker used by the retrieval flow. | You can set a full triplet, only some of its fields, or none at all — any field left unset falls back to the matching `DEFAULT_MODELS_`. So the simplest setup is to fill in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and override per-triplet fields only where they differ (e.g. `EMBED_MODEL`, `NON_REASONING_MODEL`). `*_API_KEY` also falls back to the legacy `NVIDIA_API_KEY` for backward compatibility. ## Quickstart This runs Auto-Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works

Auto-Ontology works in three stages: it generates an ontology, people certify it, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology holds three kinds of definition: - **Terms.** Business concepts such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, each with a description and synonyms, mapped to the columns that hold them. - **SQL attributes.** Reviewed SQL expressions under a term, such as a margin or a rolling total. The agent reuses them, so answers compute each measure the same way. - **Relationships.** How tables join, including bridge tables, inferred from keys and from the data. **Generate.** The ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases: 1. Read sources: extract schemas, profile columns, and sample values into the catalog. 2. Name entities: extract terms table by table and map each to columns. 3. Resolve relationships: infer joins between tables and bridge tables, and suggest SQL attributes from query history. 4. Write the ontology: store terms, relationships, and SQL attributes in Postgres, with embeddings in pgvector for retrieval. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Certify.** People make the draft trustworthy: 1. Test with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. 2. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API. 3. Certify names, descriptions, and SQL attributes once they're correct. **Answer.** For each question, the agent: 1. Classifies the intent and extracts the entities the question names. 2. Retrieves candidate terms, columns, and SQL attributes by embedding search. 3. Writes SQL from those candidates. 4. Checks the filter values and the query against the database, repairing the SQL when a check fails. 5. Runs the query and returns the answer with its SQL and the steps it took. When the candidates can't support a query, the agent reports that the question can't be answered from this data. Predictive questions go to KumoRFM when it's configured (see [Predictions](#predictions)). In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as CSV, or read them as a chart:

Auto-Ontology is compatible with [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/), the open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a [converter for Auto-Ontology](https://github.com/apache/ossie-converters/tree/main/nvidia), which Auto-Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML. Use **Settings → Import / Export**, or `POST /api/model/import` and `POST /api/model/export`. | Component | Technology | Role | Port | | ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---- | | Frontend | Next.js, Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI, authentication, public API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Text-to-SQL agent, catalog, ontology APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion service | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingestion and semantic compilation | 3002 | | MCP server | FastMCP | Read-only agent tools over the public API | 3003 | | Postgres + pgvector | PostgreSQL 17 | Catalog, ontology, app data, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Connection credential storage | n/a | Keep ports 3001 and 3002 on a private network. FastAPI trusts the user identity the frontend forwards in the `x-auto-ontology-user-id` header, and the ingestion service's endpoints (ingest, delete, reset, compile) have no authentication of their own. Clients go through the web app on port 3000. ## Use it from your agent ### MCP server The [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server gives any MCP client read-only tools over the ontology. Each user signs in through Auto-Ontology, and every call runs with that user's permissions. | Job | Tools | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | Readiness | `check_readiness`: can this deployment answer anything at all | | Terms | `search_terms`, `get_term`, `get_term_columns`, `get_term_sql_attributes`, `get_sql_attribute`, `describe_table` | | Answerability | `check_answerable`: does the ontology cover this question | | Questions | `ask_question`: the answer, the SQL, and the rows | Run the server against your deployment: ```bash AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \ uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp ``` Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "url": "http://localhost:3003/mcp" } } } ``` Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), bridged with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "command": "npx", "args": ["mcp-remote", "http://localhost:3003/mcp"] } } } ``` Restart the client after editing its config, then sign in when it prompts. Sign-in, configuration, and troubleshooting are in [docs/mcp.md](./docs/mcp.md). ### Agent skills Three skills teach a coding agent to work with Auto-Ontology. Start at [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md). | Skill | Covers | | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | [`nvidia-ontology-setup`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/) | Install, connect sources, compile, prove readiness | | [`nvidia-ontology-management`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-management/) | Inspect, model, certify, import/export, and publish | | [`nvidia-ontology-query`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-query/) | Ask questions and validate the SQL, rows, and answer | ### REST API Ask a question with `POST /api/chat/completions` on the web app's origin. Mint an API token under the user menu → **API Tokens**. The response is a server-sent event stream: a `result` event carries the answer, and `data: [DONE]` ends the stream. ```bash curl -N http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions \ -H "x-api-key: $AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}' ``` ```python import json import os import requests response = requests.post( "http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions", headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN"]}, json={"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}, stream=True, timeout=900, ) response.raise_for_status() for line in response.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True): if not line or not line.startswith("data:"): continue payload = line.removeprefix("data:").strip() if payload == "[DONE]": break event = json.loads(payload) if event["type"] == "result": print(event["answer"]["response"]) print(event["answer"]["sql_code"]) elif event["type"] == "error": raise RuntimeError(event["message"]) ``` Event types, multi-turn conversations, and the gateway trust boundary are in [docs/conversation-api.md](./docs/conversation-api.md). Every other operation is in the [OpenAPI spec](./docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json). ## Connectors, models, and predictions ### Sources Auto-Ontology connects to ten engines: - PostgreSQL - MySQL - Databricks - Snowflake - ClickHouse - Trino - Apache Kyuubi - HeavyDB - DuckDB - SQLite Add connections under **Settings → Connections**, or list them in `CONNECTION_STRINGS`. DuckDB and SQLite are connection-string only. See [docs/connections.md](./docs/connections.md) for URL schemes, scoping, and credential storage. ### Models Auto-Ontology uses four model roles. With an `nvapi-` key, each defaults to an NVIDIA NIM on [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com): | Role | Default model | What it does | | --------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `REASONING` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` | Builds the ontology (terms, relationships, SQL attributes), writes each answer's SQL and explanation, and grades answerability | | `NON_REASONING` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` | Runs the agent's faster steps: question intent, entity extraction, candidate selection, and SQL checks and repair | | `EMBED` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-embed-1b` | Indexes tables, columns, terms, and SQL attributes in pgvector, and matches each question to them | | `RERANK` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-rerank-8b` | Ranks candidate tables when compilation builds bridge-table SQL attributes | To use self-hosted NIM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set `_ENDPOINT`, `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`. Any field you leave unset falls back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_`, so the simplest setup fills in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and overrides only what differs. Use models that support structured output, and keep the embedding model the same for ingestion and queries. [`.env.example`](./.env.example) documents every variable. ### Predictions Set `KUMO_RFM_API_KEY` and the agent routes predictive questions to KumoRFM. KumoRFM is a hosted service: to answer, the agent uploads the connected tables to it, capped by `KUMO_MAX_TABLES` (20 by default) and `KUMO_MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE` (unlimited unless set). Review what that sends, and complete your organization's data review, before you enable it. ## Integrate with us To integrate an agent platform, application, or storage provider with Auto-Ontology, [open an integration request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology/issues/new?template=integration.yml). The Auto-Ontology team maintains the code and doesn't accept external pull requests. Integration requests and bug reports are welcome as issues. Report security vulnerabilities through [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md). Maintainer workflow is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Reference | Topic | Doc | | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | Kubernetes deployment with Helm | [DEPLOYMENT.md](./DEPLOYMENT.md) | | Connections, scoping, and Vault | [docs/connections.md](./docs/connections.md) | | Authentication, SSO, and API tokens | [docs/authentication.md](./docs/authentication.md) | | Conversation API | [docs/conversation-api.md](./docs/conversation-api.md) | | MCP server | [docs/mcp.md](./docs/mcp.md) | | REST API | [docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json](./docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json) | ## License Auto-Ontology is licensed under the [Apache License, Version 2.0](./LICENSE). Components added by the container images are listed separately in [`CONTAINER_THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./CONTAINER_THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Notice and Disclaimer NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER: This software automatically retrieves, accesses or interacts with external materials. # Skills For Real Engineers [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/mattpocock/skills)](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) My agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding. Developing real applications is hard. Approaches like GSD, BMAD, and Spec-Kit try to help by owning the process. But while doing so, they take away your control and make bugs in the process hard to resolve. These skills are designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable. They work with any model. They're based on decades of engineering experience. Hack around with them. Make them your own. Enjoy. If you want to keep up with changes to these skills, and any new ones I create, you can join ~60,000 other devs on my newsletter: [Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://www.aihero.dev/s/skills-newsletter) ## Installation (30-second setup) A plugin updates itself. [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/mattpocock/skills) copies editable files into your project, and you update them by hand. Pick one per agent, because installing both gives you every skill twice. ### 1. Get the skills
Claude Code ```bash claude plugin install mattpocock-skills@claude-plugins-official ``` Updates itself by default.
Codex ```bash codex plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills codex plugin add mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Updates itself at startup.
GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code) ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add mattpocock/skills copilot plugin install mattpocock-skills@mattpocock ``` Then, once, add to `~/.copilot/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "mattpocock": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "mattpocock/skills" }, "autoUpdate": true } } } ``` In VS Code, run **Chat: Install Plugin From Source** and enter `https://github.com/mattpocock/skills`. It updates daily.
Gemini CLI (manual updates) ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/engineering gemini skills install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills.git --path skills/productivity ``` Re-run both commands to update.
Any other agent, or editable files (manual updates) ```bash npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills -a # cursor, opencode, devin, windsurf, amp, pi; omit -a to choose ``` When the installer asks which skills to take, include `setup-matt-pocock-skills`. To update, run `npx skills@latest update`, and re-run `add` to pick up new skills.
### 2. Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` In your agent, run it once per repo. It will: - Ask you which issue tracker you want to use (GitHub, GitLab, local files, or anything else you describe) - Ask you what labels you apply to tickets when you triage them (`/triage` uses labels) - Ask you where you want to save any docs we create ### 3. Bam - you're ready to go. ## Why These Skills Exist I built these skills as a way to fix common failure modes I see with Claude Code, Codex, and other coding agents. ### #1: The Agent Didn't Do What I Want > "No-one knows exactly what they want" > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**. The most common failure mode in software development is misalignment. You think the dev knows what you want. Then you see what they've built - and you realize it didn't understand you at all. This is just the same in the AI age. There is a communication gap between you and the agent. The fix for this is a **grilling session** - getting the agent to ask you detailed questions about what you're building. **The Fix** is to use: - [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) - for non-code uses - [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md) - same as [`/grill-me`](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md), but adds more goodies (see below) These are my most popular skills. They help you align with the agent before you get started, and think deeply about the change you're making. Use them _every_ time you want to make a change. ### #2: The Agent Is Way Too Verbose > With a ubiquitous language, conversations among developers and expressions of the code are all derived from the same domain model. > > Eric Evans, [Domain-Driven-Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Domain-Driven-Design-Tackling-Complexity-Software/dp/0321125215) **The Problem**: At the start of a project, devs and the people they're building the software for (the domain experts) are usually speaking different languages. I felt the same tension with my agents. Agents are usually dropped into a project and asked to figure out the jargon as they go. So they use 20 words where 1 will do. **The Fix** for this is a shared language. It's a document that helps agents decode the jargon used in the project.
Example Here's an example [glossary](https://github.com/mattpocock/course-video-manager/blob/076a5a7a182db0fe1e62971dd7a68bcadf010f1c/CONTEXT.md) (still named `CONTEXT.md` at that pinned commit, from before the skills renamed the convention), from my `course-video-manager` repo. Which one is easier to read? - **BEFORE**: "There's a problem when a lesson inside a section of a course is made 'real' (i.e. given a spot in the file system)" - **AFTER**: "There's a problem with the materialization cascade" This concision pays off session after session.
This is built into [`/grill-with-docs`](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md). It's a grilling session, but that helps you build a shared language with the AI, and document hard-to-explain decisions in ADR's. It's hard to explain how powerful this is. It might be the single coolest technique in this repo. Try it, and see. > [!TIP] > A shared language has many other benefits than reducing verbosity: > > - **Variables, functions and files are named consistently**, using the shared language > - As a result, the **codebase is easier to navigate** for the agent > - The agent also **spends fewer tokens on thinking**, because it has access to a more concise language ### #3: The Code Doesn't Work > "Always take small, deliberate steps. The rate of feedback is your speed limit. Never take on a task that’s too big." > > David Thomas & Andrew Hunt, [The Pragmatic Programmer](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Pragmatic-Programmer-Anniversary-Journey-Mastery/dp/B0833F1T3V) **The Problem**: Let's say that you and the agent are aligned on what to build. What happens when the agent _still_ produces crap? It's time to look at your feedback loops. Without feedback on how the code it produces actually runs, the agent will be flying blind. **The Fix**: You need the usual tranche of feedback loops: static types, browser access, and automated tests. For automated tests, a red-green-refactor loop is critical. This is where the agent writes a failing test first, then fixes the test. This helps give the agent a consistent level of feedback that results in far better code. I've built a **[`/tdd`](./skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md) skill** you can slot into any project. It encourages red-green-refactor and gives the agent plenty of guidance on what makes good and bad tests. For debugging, I've also built a **[`/diagnosing-bugs`](./skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)** skill that wraps best debugging practices into a disciplined loop, gated phase by phase. ### #4: We Built A Ball Of Mud > "Invest in the design of the system _every day_." > > Kent Beck, [Extreme Programming Explained](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Extreme-Programming-Explained-Embrace-Change/dp/0321278658) > "The best modules are deep. They allow a lot of functionality to be accessed through a simple interface." > > John Ousterhout, [A Philosophy Of Software Design](https://www.amazon.co.uk/Philosophy-Software-Design-2nd/dp/173210221X) **The Problem**: Most apps built with agents are complex and hard to change. Because agents can radically speed up coding, they also accelerate software entropy. Codebases get more complex at an unprecedented rate. **The Fix** for this is a radical new approach to AI-powered development: caring about the design of the code. This is built in to every layer of these skills: - [`/to-spec`](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md) quizzes you about which modules you're touching before creating a spec And crucially, [`/improve-codebase-architecture`](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md) surveys a codebase for deepening opportunities and hands you the candidates. I recommend running it on your codebase once every few days. It is a survey, not a rescue: on a genuinely old codebase it will find real candidates, but it won't untangle the mud for you. ### Summary Software engineering fundamentals matter more than ever. These skills are my best effort at condensing these fundamentals into repeatable practices, to help you ship the best apps of your career. Enjoy. ## Reference These split on one axis: who can invoke them. **User-invoked** skills are reachable only when you type them (e.g. `/grill-me`); their job is to orchestrate. **Model-invoked** skills can be invoked by you _or_ reached for automatically by the agent when the task fits; they hold the reusable discipline. A user-invoked skill may invoke model-invoked skills, but never another user-invoked one. ### Engineering Skills I use daily for code work. **User-invoked** - **[ask-matt](./skills/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md)**: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the user-invoked skills in this repo. - **[grill-with-docs](./skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md)**: Grilling session that also builds your project's domain model, sharpening terminology and updating `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline. - **[triage](./skills/engineering/triage/SKILL.md)**: Move issues through a state machine of triage roles. - **[improve-codebase-architecture](./skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md)**: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick. - **[setup-matt-pocock-skills](./skills/engineering/setup-matt-pocock-skills/SKILL.md)**: Configure this repo for the engineering skills (issue tracker, triage labels, domain doc layout). Run once per repo before using the other engineering skills. - **[to-spec](./skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md)**: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the issue tracker. No interview, just synthesizes what you've already discussed. - **[to-tickets](./skills/engineering/to-tickets/SKILL.md)**: Break any plan, spec, or conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, written as text in a local file, or as native blocking links on a real tracker. - **[implement](./skills/engineering/implement/SKILL.md)**: Build the work described by a spec or set of tickets, driving `/tdd` at pre-agreed seams and closing out with `/code-review` before committing. - **[implement-spec](./skills/engineering/implement-spec/SKILL.md)**: Implement a whole spec on one integration branch. Works the tickets as a task graph, running implementer subagents across the ready frontier for maximum concurrency, then closes out with `/code-review`. - **[wayfinder](./skills/engineering/wayfinder/SKILL.md)**: Plan a huge chunk of work, more than one agent session can hold, as a shared map of decision tickets on the issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear. - **[retro](./skills/engineering/retro/SKILL.md)**: Suggest improvements to the coding agent's environment (navigation, automated checks, coding standards, steering files, tooling) after a session, most severe first. **Model-invoked** - **[prototype](./skills/engineering/prototype/SKILL.md)**: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question, either a single shareable HTML file for state/logic questions, or several radically different UI variations toggleable from one route. - **[diagnosing-bugs](./skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md)**: Disciplined diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions: build a feedback loop that goes red on this bug → minimise → hypothesise → instrument → fix → regression-test. - **[research](./skills/engineering/research/SKILL.md)**: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a cited Markdown file in the repo, run as a background agent. - **[tdd](./skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md)**: Test-driven development with a red-green-refactor loop. Builds features or fixes bugs one vertical slice at a time. - **[domain-modeling](./skills/engineering/domain-modeling/SKILL.md)**: Actively build and sharpen a project's domain model: challenge terms against the glossary, stress-test with edge-case scenarios, and update `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs inline. - **[codebase-design](./skills/engineering/codebase-design/SKILL.md)**: Shared discipline and vocabulary for designing deep modules: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. - **[code-review](./skills/engineering/code-review/SKILL.md)**: Two-axis review of the diff since a fixed point: **Standards** (does it follow the repo's coding standards, plus a Fowler smell baseline?) and **Spec** (does it faithfully implement the originating issue/spec?), run as parallel sub-agents so neither pollutes the other. - **[pr](./skills/engineering/pr/SKILL.md)**: The shape a pull request body should take: a summary as the smallest visual that makes the change clear, before/after evidence that it works, and a merge-danger call (one-way or two-way door, plus blast radius). - **[wizard](./skills/engineering/wizard/SKILL.md)**: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform: provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. ### Productivity General workflow tools, not code-specific. **User-invoked** - **[grill-me](./skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md)**: Get relentlessly interviewed about a plan or design until every branch of the design tree is resolved. - **[handoff](./skills/productivity/handoff/SKILL.md)**: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document so another agent can continue the work. - **[teach](./skills/productivity/teach/SKILL.md)**: Teach the user a new skill or concept over multiple sessions, using the current directory as a stateful teaching workspace. - **[to-questionnaire](./skills/productivity/to-questionnaire/SKILL.md)**: Turn a decision you can't answer alone into a Markdown questionnaire for the one person who can, filled in async, or together over a meeting. It grills you about the send (who it's for, what you need back), not the subject. - **[wait-what](./skills/productivity/wait-what/SKILL.md)**: Fire this the moment a message doesn't land. The agent re-pitches it with the context you're missing, in plain English, using your `GLOSSARY.md` vocabulary. **Model-invoked** - **[grilling](./skills/productivity/grilling/SKILL.md)**: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea until every branch of the design tree is resolved. The reusable interview primitive behind `grill-me`, `grill-with-docs`, `triage`, `wayfinder` and `improve-codebase-architecture`. - **[writing-for-agents](./skills/productivity/writing-for-agents/SKILL.md)**: Writing documents for agents: skills, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and any doc an agent reaches by a pointer.

# Lieflat Less AI Tone

中文 | [English](README.en.md)

![去 AI 味 Skill：约 520 万字、100+ 项指标、约 50 万次模型语义判断](assets/less-ai-tone-hero-zh.png)

**一个基于两轮实测语料（共 1,169 篇、约 520 万汉字、100+ 项指标、约 50 万次模型语义判断）的去 AI 味 skill：先交付有指标、研究参照、原文例句和改法的检测报告，用户回复后再改写和复测。**

这个 skill 用两轮对照研究筛选值得处理的写作特征，再对成稿做有依据的检测和最小改写。

---

## 1 研究问题

AI 在 Coding 能力提升的同时，写作的体感好像并没有同步变好，生成的文字依然读起来很奇怪。

比如不少主力模型智商极高，但写出来的长文我往往要读好几遍，很大的原因是它满篇都在用「不是技术问题，而是认知问题」的对举、密集的破折号和分号，还有完全理解不了的比喻。

为了处理这些问题，常见的做法是给模型列一张禁用词表，或者塞一段「去 AI 味 Prompt」。我也试过很长一段时间，但实操下来有两个明显痛点：

第一是禁用词表管不住真正的 AI 味。很多文章完全避开了「赋能」「闭环」「抓手」，标点也很克制，但读完三段依然一眼就能看出是 AI 写的。

第二是容易乱改、误伤正常表达。把十几条经验规则攒在一起喂给模型直接改稿，模型会非常激进地把文章里原本自然的设问句、「一、二、三」小标题一并删掉，甚至为了迎合「长短句参差」的指令，把顺畅的句子硬生生拆碎。

市面上流传的「AI 味清单」基本来自个案观察和个人语感，从未经过系统检验。我的思路是，从「读着像 AI」这个很难直接验证的主观体验里，找到若干个能客观反映模型写作特征的指标，先量化评测，再顺藤摸瓜地从工程和规则上把问题解决掉。

从源头看，把「去 AI 味」做成一套可靠的 Skill，核心只涉及三个问题：

第一，怎么把脚本数不出来的「AI 味」真正测准？这决定了能不能抓到藏在句子意思和上下文里的深层习惯。

第二，哪些语言特征是真正影响阅读体验的标准？这决定了改写规则往哪里发力。

第三，拿到这些指标后，如何管住模型的手？这决定了改写过程能否在清理套路的同时，不误伤作者原本的正常表达。

这些工作在构建思路上有两个相同的原则：

首先是有效，让每个指标能简洁直接地对应一个可定位的句法或篇章问题，通过指标高低，顺藤摸瓜地在规则上准确动刀。

其次是可靠，让评测与改写前后的变化尽量可以量化，避免凭感觉盲改。

## 2 两轮实验

### 2.1 第一轮实验：629 篇对照文本

语料生成方法：同一批话题，五个模型各写 60 篇，与 329 篇人类作者文章对照。

语料统计：

| 侧 | 篇 | 汉字 | 句 | 段 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 生成 | 300 | 1,179,105 | 37,642 | 14,549 |
| 人类 | 329 | 1,647,867 | 57,909 | 31,172 |

模型：claude-opus-4-6、deepseek-v4-pro、gemini-3.1-pro、gpt-5.6-sol、kimi-k3。人类侧分组独立统计，检验组间一致性。

判定标准： 倍率 R = 生成侧频率 ÷ 人类侧频率。R≥2.0 纳入；1.25–2.0 条件纳入（需人类侧组间一致且绝对量足）；0.8–1.25 排除；<0.8 人类更多，反向也不可作为删改依据。另有三项附加条件：组间一致性（极差≤5 倍）、算子可定位性（能指出改哪一句）、改写可操作性（"补虚词"无法验收，整项弃用）。

### 2.2 第二轮实验：270 对配对复测

第一轮实验的根本缺陷是语料不配对，第二轮收紧了这一点，选择将人类文章里的数字、事件提炼成任务卡发给 AI，让它在同样的事实约束下写同题文章。

三层测量标准：脚本层，语义层和人工层。脚本层用正则数标点个数、句长、小节数等完全可被量化计算的部分。语义层补充脚本层无法判断的语义理解部分，脚本先抽候选片段，模型对每条做封闭式判断（这是不是密集并列/结论宣告/结构复用），在这里使用 Jev 进行判断，总共判断50 万次。最后是人工测评层面。

一个特征在某一层测量中显著即可成立，不需要三层全通过。

| 层 | 工具 | 测什么 | 规模 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 脚本层 | Python 正则 + 统计 | 90 项可计算指标：标点密度、句长分布、词汇多样性（mtld/mattr）、欧化构式、小节几何、段落桥接、正式度波动、四字词、黑名单词 | 540 篇全量，配对 Wilcoxon + Cliff's δ，\|δ\|≥0.33 显著 |
| 语义层 | 结构化判断接口（Jev） | 9 项脚本测不了的语义指标：结论提示冒号、密集并列、序数词小标题、相邻句同构、段首零回指、句间段间衔接、"这意味着"复述、概括替代具体信息、拟人化喻体 + 活跃暗喻密度 | **约 50 万次判断**（第二轮 43.1 万 + 增补轮回指/同义重命名约 11 万）、1.92 万次请求、3.54 亿 token，全部落盘可复算 |
| 人工层 | 逐句标注 + 抽样复核 | 比喻贴切度、判据误判率 | AI 比喻失败模式归纳（硬套宏大意象、直译腔、混合比喻、三连标题） |

## 3 核心结果：最终指标汇总

按证据强度分四层。表中同时列出第一轮对照值和第二轮配对复测结果，并标明所属口径；配对复测的脚本层使用配对 Wilcoxon + Cliff's δ（|δ|≥0.33 为显著门槛），语义层约 50 万次模型判断。

δ 是什么：随机抽一篇 AI 文和一篇人类文对比，「AI 更多」的概率减去「AI 更少」的概率。正数=AI 比人类多，负数=AI 比人类少；绝对值越大差距越大，0.33 以上算显著，0.66 以上算差距很大。

### 3.1 第一层：通用显著 AI 味指标

由脚本层/语义层/人工层共同测出、GPT5.6 和 Opus4.6 同向显著的9条指标如下：

| 特征 | 脚本层证据（GPT δ / Opus δ） | 语义层证据 | 方向 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **欧化构式「不是A而是B」** | +0.88 / +0.72（最强纯写作信号） | 密集并列 1.45 倍 | 生成侧多。例：「用户购买的不是模型参数，而是一件每天要戴、需要充电、还会出现在社交场合的物品」「潘宇扬并不是从通用AI退回一个小功能，而是在尝试证明另一种生长顺序」 |
| **用词不敢重复（mtld/mattr）** | +0.91/+0.55、+0.75/+0.55 | — | 生成侧词汇更多样。例：同一段里「优化／增强／提升／提高」轮着用；「采用兼容体系……站点利用率就可能提升」——人类会反复用同一个词，AI 换着说 |
| **结构切得太碎** | 小节长度方差 −0.91/−0.75、小标题密度 +0.65/+0.83、每节句数 −0.63/−0.79、小节数 +0.51/+0.70（中位数 AI 7 vs 人类 1） | —（分节是纯结构特征，语义层不测） | 生成侧分节多而短且整齐。实测抽样：AI 文 1.3–1.7 个小标题/千字（3000–6000 字的文章切 5–9 节），人类整篇连写、按自然话题换段 |
| **句长/节奏太均匀** | 句长方差 −0.88/−0.40、逗号小句长方差 −0.87(GPT) | — | 生成侧落差小。第一轮抽样中 AI 文句长 CV 0.41–0.55、人类 0.67；配对复测的人类参考值为 0.54，两轮口径不可直接混用，也不能据此机械调整句长 |
| **前置定语长（欧化）** | +0.48 / +0.54 | — | 生成侧名词前修饰长。例：「它还不是一套能够在任何餐桌上完全自动运行的系统」「这种连续数据也解释了为什么团队没有把产品做成一次拍照识别的工具」——中心词前面挂了二十来字的修饰 |
| **结论提示冒号** | 冒号总密度人类反而多（−0.37/−0.31） | 「结论提示」AI 2.1 倍（「核心是：」「残酷的现实是：」） | 生成侧爱先摆结论。例：「这组数字传递出一个残酷的现实：不管你是街边个体户的夫妻店……三个月是第一道坎，半年是生死线」 |
| **衔接过度顺滑** | — | AI 明确承接 98.9% vs 人类 95.2%；段间跳转 AI 2.1% vs 人类 7.2% | 生成侧段段紧扣。例：连续多段以「这也解释了为什么……」「从这个角度看……」开头（实测 30 篇里"这也解释了"起段 10 次）；人类每 14 段就有一次直接跳到新话题，AI 每 50 段才一次 |
| **密集并列/枚举** | 顿号 +0.56(GPT)、分号 +0.80(GPT) | AI 7.845 vs 人类 5.398 每千字（1.45 倍） | 生成侧爱排比列举。例：「火锅、快餐、家庭聚餐和独自进食，不同光线、不同穿着、……」一句连排多个场景维度 |
| **比喻贴切度差** | —（正则只能数比喻标记词，标记词密度人类反而多 2.4 倍） | —（六个大模型两两共识仅 0–40%，最高分段 22 句里 9 句误报——测不出是模型能力缺口，不是信号不存在） | **人工层确证**。失败模式：硬套宏大意象（"窄门""三根支柱"）、直译腔（"钢夹"）、混合比喻（"坠崖＋松动地板"）、三连标题。贴切度只能人审；skill 默认保留原文比喻 |

**一次重要的二次否决**：初次语义测评发现 24.7% 的可比较段落从具体信息变得更概括，曾据此设立改写规则。改用对称口径复查后，向相反方向变化的比例为 26.0%，净差近零；精确数字密度在配对复测中也无差异。因此“概括替代”已从改写规则降为 X 级，不再据此删改。原文事实和限定词仍受信息守恒原则保护。

### 3.2 第二层：不同模型有不同的写作特征

特征本质是高度重复的表层习惯，即标点与句法的使用偏好，包括破折号用多少、句子多长、爱不爱分号等。这类指标，判定证据主要来自脚本验证。主要有以下特征指标：

| 特征 | GPT-5.6 | Claude Opus 4.6 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 破折号 | −0.54（比人类还少） | **+0.95**（100% 文章使用） | 方向完全相反，改写必须先知道文本像谁。Opus 例：「在营收急剧收缩的压力下，公司迅速启动了大规模的营销开支削减——最先被砍掉的，正是搜索广告和效果投放」 |
| 每小句「的」字 | −0.75 | +0.62 | GPT「的」用得比人类少，Opus 比人类多，方向相反 |
| 引号 | ≈0 | −0.67 | Opus 写文章明显不爱用引号，比人类少得多 |
| 分号 / 顿号 | +0.80 / +0.56 | −0.11 / +0.14 | GPT 专属。例：「对于食材分明的欧美常见"白人餐"，准确率可以超过90%；到了中餐火锅，准确率约为70%至80%；遇到糊状食物，则需要用户通过语音或事后手动补充」——三档场景用两个分号串成一句，人类更常拆成三句 |
| 句子结构绕（单动词句少等） | 全显著 | 全不显著 | GPT 专属，含三个子特征，各配例：**① 单动词句少**（δ−0.72）——一个动词撑一句的短直句（「转折发生在疫情期间。」「Odyss试图把这一步交给机器。」）在 GPT 文中稀少，取而代之的是动词堆叠：「项链利用多模态视觉大模型，观察食物被送入口中的过程，再把零散的进食动作还原成一天的饮食记录」——一句四个动词连环。**② 静态句少**（δ−0.71）——直陈状态/判断的句子（「问题在于，开发者影响力不等于消费者入口。」）人类常用，GPT 偏爱把一切都写成动作过程。**③ 主谓距离短**（δ−0.62）——人类常在主语和谓语之间插一大段：「续航能否覆盖一天，设备是否舒适，记录是否准确，建议是否真的改变饮食，这些问题只有在持续使用中才会显现」——主语到谓语隔了 30 字，GPT 很少这样写 |
| 少提问 | −0.59 | −0.12 | GPT 写文章明显不爱提问，比人类少得多；Opus 跟人类差不多 |
| 长句少/中句多 | −0.68/+0.81 | +0.05/+0.04 | GPT 写长句比人类少、中句比人类多：句长集中在中档（25–45 字），几乎没有 6–12 字的短促句收尾，也极少 60 字以上的长流水句 |
| 焦点后置 | +0.05 | +0.47 | Opus 专属：新信息压在句尾，铺垫占前大半句。「定价权不在工厂手里，品牌归属也不在工厂手里，工厂只是全球供应链上那个沉默的、可以被随时替换的生产节点」「如果说一个行业每天有近一万间门店关门，听起来像是危言耸听，但这恰恰是中国餐饮业正在发生的事」——读者要等最后才知道这句想说什么 |
| **活跃暗喻密度** | 2.099 ≈ 人类 2.066 | **2.851**（合并口径 1.2 倍全部由 Opus 拉高） | Opus 专属的研究观察，不是通用删改依据。GPT 暗喻量与人类无异；两种模型的比喻贴切度都需要人审，skill 默认保留原文比喻 |

| 特征 | 证据 |

| 相邻句高度同构 | AI 8.71% vs 5.52%（1.6 倍，三连句 2.75 倍） |

## 4 工作流

```bash
# 第一步：脚本检测（只报告，不改写；--json 存档供第四步用）
python3 scripts/detect.py <文件或目录> --json > /tmp/before.json

# 第 1.5 步：语义层候选抽取 + 会话内模型按封闭判据判读
#   （同义重命名段 / 段间衔接接口 / 冒号句 / 三连同构组，
#     判据见 references/semantic-criteria.md，单篇约 40-80 条）
python3 scripts/detect.py <文件> --candidates --out /tmp/candidates.json

# 第二步：模型复核命中，报告本篇指标、研究显著性、例句、改法和排除项；等待用户回复

# 第三步：收到用户回复后，按其接受或调整的方案改写（规则见 SKILL.md）

# 第四步：复测 + 前后对比报告（默认 Markdown，--format html 出网页版）
python3 scripts/detect.py <改后文件> --json > /tmp/after.json
python3 scripts/report.py 原文 改后文 /tmp/before.json /tmp/after.json \
    --semantic /tmp/candidates_labeled.json --out 去AI味报告.md
```

完整示例：[Agent 记忆问题案例](examples/agent-memory-case/README.md)。其中有改前报告、改后全文、左右两列 HTML 对照页和复测结论。

检测分三层：**脚本层**（数得出符号的，detect.py）、**语义层**（要理解句意的四项，会话内模型按封闭判据逐条判）、**人审层**（比喻贴切度/暗喻/拟人喻体——模型间共识只有 0-40%，只列出不判）。

检测报告分级：

| 级 | 含义 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| A | 机械改：删提示语、换标点，零语义风险 | 模型复核误报并提出建议；用户回复后改 |
| B | 建议改：顿号罗列、长定语，需句式重组 | 模型逐条筛选并提出建议；用户回复后改 |
| C | 只报告：句长均匀、结构碎——整篇级问题 | 默认不改；用户主动要求时再处理 |
| H | 人审区：拟人喻体等贴切度问题，模型判不准 | 默认保留；用户主动要求时再列清单 |
| X | 已否决：实测不是 AI 味（配对复测反向） | 永不改，展示计数防误改 |
| F | 指纹：破折号/分号/引号等分模型特征 | 带方向解读；可安全改写的局部命中默认建议改，保留须给具体理由 |

### 防过度改写

模型改写 AI 味最常见的失败是改过头：为"像人写的"把句子改得忽长忽短、拆段落、删掉本来正常的表达。SKILL.md 定了六条改写原则：**最小改动**（一处命中只改必需部分）、**信息守恒**（改写后每个实词须能在原文指出出处）、**不制造参差**（句长离散度人机无差异，不为节奏改句长）、**结构不动**、有风格参考时以参考为准、改后三查加复测。

检测报告的结构区（句长 CV、节长 CV、同构/百段、小标题密度）会标明各参考值所属轮次与计算口径。配对复测的句长 CV 人类参考值为 0.54；第一轮抽样的 0.67 不与其混用，也不把任何指标强行推到目标值——机械参差化比不改更糟。

## 7 局限

1. 语义层是单模型判断，抽样复核误判 15–30%，方向可信、精确百分点不可信
2. 人类语料组间差异大（破折号极差百倍），扩充语料可能改变部分结论
3. 模型迭代持续向人类文风收敛，所有频率数值是特定时点观测
4. 比喻贴切度、案例是否凑数、参差的质量，机器测不了，只能人审

---

## 8 安装与使用

让支持 Agent Skills 的 AI 安装仓库中的 `lieflat-less-ai-tone` skill；也可以在本机运行：

```bash
npx skills add larashero3-dotcom/lieflat-less-ai-tone
```

安装后给 AI 一篇成稿。它会先运行脚本并判读语义候选，交付有研究参照、原文例句和具体改法的检测报告。你回复「按建议改」或调整范围后，它才改写、复测并生成前后对比。完整演示见 [Agent 记忆问题案例](./examples/agent-memory-case/README.md)。

Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

The AI Orchestrator for 100x builders.
Run Claude Code, Codex, and any other coding agent in parallel, each in its own worktree. Chat or terminal, on your laptop or in the cloud, with diffs, a browser, and a CLI in one app.

Download Orca

## Features
### Orchestrate Agents Hand a big task to one agent. It splits the work, starts worker agents in their own workspaces, and brings their results back to you. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration)
### Chat or Terminal Run any agent in Chat UI or as the raw CLI, and move a conversation between the two without losing context. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/agents/native-chat)
### Run Anywhere Pair a Remote Orca Server, work on any SSH host, or give a worktree its own cloud VM. Your agents keep running when your laptop sleeps. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/ways-to-run)
### Mobile App Pair Orca with the mobile app to get pinged when an agent needs you, reply in chat, and keep work moving on any of your machines when you are away from your desk. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Android APK](https://www.onorca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Review AI Output Review diffs, leave notes on exact changed lines, and send focused feedback back to an agent. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Git Integration Draft commit messages and pull requests from the diff, then send failing checks or PR review comments back to an agent to fix. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/commit-push)
### Parallel Worktrees Quickly split tasks into isolated environments, so multiple agents can work side by side without interfering with each other. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Design Mode Click any element in Orca's browser to copy its HTML, styles, and selector, then paste it into your agent's chat. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native See your GitHub and Linear tasks in one place, and start a workspace for each when you're ready to build. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### Orca CLI Anything you can do in Orca, your agents can do too: create worktrees, start workers, drive the browser and desktop apps, and schedule automations, all from the command line. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
### Plugins Themes, editors, languages, and panels from the community, installed in a click. [Browse plugins →](https://www.onorca.dev/plugins)
### Split Anything Put agents, terminals, browsers, and diffs side by side in split panes shaped to the task. [Docs →](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/tabs-panes-splits)
**Also in the box:** - **[Drag Files to Agents](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)**: drag files from the explorer, or images from your desktop, straight into an agent's prompt. - **[Jump Anywhere](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)**: one shortcut jumps to any workspace or tab across every repo and host. - **[Rich Previews](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/editing/viewers)**: open images, PDFs, and Markdown right in the workspace, next to the agent that made them. - **[Mobile Emulator](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/overview#mobile-emulator)**: run an iOS Simulator or Android emulator beside your agent, and let it tap, type, and check its own work. - **[Dictation](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/settings#voice)**: press a shortcut and talk. Orca types what you say into the agent's prompt or terminal. - **[Usage & Accounts](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)**: see how much of your agent limits you've used and when they reset, and switch accounts without logging out. - **[Automations](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/automations)**: schedule prompts to run on any repo: nightly dependency bumps, weekly triage, flaky-test sweeps. - **[Computer Use](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)**: when there's no CLI or API, agents can see and drive desktop apps and external browsers. - **And many, many more**: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

--- ## Install ### Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux - **[Download from onOrca.dev](https://onorca.dev/download)** - Or grab a build directly: [macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-arm64.dmg) · [macOS Intel](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-macos-x64.dmg) · [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-windows-setup.exe) · [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/orca-linux.AppImage) · [All builds](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest) _Or via a package manager:_ ```bash # macOS (Homebrew) # Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask. brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Upgrade an existing install brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca # Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source yay -S stably-orca-bin ``` ### Mobile App — iOS, Android Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone. - **iOS:** [Download on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) - **Android:** [Download APK](https://www.onorca.dev/download/android) · [Install guide](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/android-apk) --- ## Community & Support - **Discord:** Join the community on **[Discord](https://discord.gg/fzjDKHxv8Q)**. - **Twitter / X:** Follow **[@orca_build](https://x.com/orca_build)** for updates and announcements. - **WeChat:** Scan to join the Orca community WeChat group. - **Feedback & Ideas:** We ship fast. Missing something? [Request a new feature](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues). - **Privacy:** See the [privacy & telemetry docs](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/telemetry) for what anonymous usage data Orca collects and how to opt out. - **Show Support:** [Star](https://github.com/stablyai/orca) this repo to follow along with our daily ships. --- ## Developing Want to contribute or run locally? See our [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) guide.

## Signed Builds Windows code signing sponsored/provided by [SignPath.io](https://signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org). ## License Orca is free and open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

# Lichii Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. ## Downloads and setup Published builds belong on this fork's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Eglantine/releases). The repository still uses its historical Eglantine name; the desktop application is now Lichii. On Windows, extract the entire build archive and run **lichii.exe**. Only use games and system files you have legally obtained. Games, keys and firmware are not included. ### Existing saves and settings The rebrand intentionally retains the existing Eden/Eglantine data directories and configuration keys. It does not move or delete saves, settings or shader caches. Back up your saves before testing experimental builds. ## Compatibility and issue reports Compatibility and performance vary by game, hardware and driver. Rendering errors, stutters and crashes remain possible. Passing automated tests does not establish that a game renders correctly, and this project makes no universal frame-rate guarantee. When [reporting an issue](https://github.com/zortos293/Eglantine/issues), include: - The exact build, game version, CPU, GPU and driver version. - Relevant settings and steps to reproduce the problem. - A screenshot and the log from the affected session, after checking it for personal information. Do not upload game files, keys, firmware or private account information. ## Building and contributing See the [build guide](docs/Build.md), [user documentation](docs/user/README.md) and [coding guidelines](docs/Coding.md). Some inherited documentation and internal build target names still use upstream names. The GUI build target remains `yuzu`; its output is `lichii.exe` on Windows and `lichii` on other desktop platforms. Keep changes focused and distinguish code-level checks from actual gameplay testing. ## Artwork Art created by YOB (yobslab) The supplied Lichii logo, icon and library artwork are in [dist/branding](dist/branding). Windows, Linux and macOS icon resources are generated from that artwork by [Generate-LichiiIcons.ps1](tools/Generate-LichiiIcons.ps1). ## Support Lichii Lichii is free and stays free. If you want to help, you can donate in crypto. 简体中文 · English

DeepSeek Harness 的 Android 客户端。手机上直接跑，也能遥控你电脑上的 DSH。


Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30


Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活

干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。


下载 DSH Go

从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。

 

感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱，我将尽快适配 iOS 和鸿蒙！大家 Star 点得越多，我适配得越快哦 hhh

第一次用可以先看使用指南，遇到问题欢迎来论坛和 QQ 群。
手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。


本机运行，也能遥控电脑

内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。


插话、打断，过程自动收好

回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。


原生界面，也有网页版

和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。


分享卡、对话回放和链接

回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。


横屏与平板

横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。


主题配色与桌面图标

六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。


中文，也说 English

全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。


手机操控

看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。


## 可以做什么 DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。 - **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。 - **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。 - **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。 - **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。 - **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。 - **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。 功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。 ## 安装 安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。 1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。 2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。 3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。 仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。 本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。 ## 数据与权限 模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。 “发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。 ## 风险提示与免责声明 DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，也不代表 DeepSeek。使用前请了解： - **AI 并非万无一失**：回答、代码和操作可能出错，也可能被网页、消息或文件中的恶意指令误导。请核验重要结果；医疗、法律、投资等高风险决策不应仅依赖 AI 输出。 - **工具会产生真实影响**：本机或远程主机上的命令、文件修改及手机操控可能导致数据丢失、隐私泄露、账号、资金或设备损失。免确认、放宽应用规则或解除限制会减少保护；确认与拦截机制不能保证消除所有风险。建议保留默认保护，只授予必要权限，不在存有支付或银行信息的设备上解除限制。详见[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。 - **第三方服务与费用**：模型、远程主机和插件等按各自条款运行；相关数据处理、服务可用性和费用取决于你选择的服务与配置。本机运行不等于模型离线，也不代表数据不会离开设备。 - **使用前做好防护**：备份重要数据，只连接可信主机、安装可信插件，留意模型用量与费用；不要让 AI 无人值守地处理不可逆或高风险任务。 - **无担保与责任范围**：在适用法律允许的范围内，本软件按“现状”提供，不保证准确性、持续可用性或满足特定用途；相关无担保及责任限制见 [LICENSE](LICENSE) 第 15–17 条。本声明不排除或限制依法不得排除或限制的责任，也不减损你依法享有的权利。 ## 常见问题
和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？
没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。
安全吗？
本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。
切到后台会被杀吗？
部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。
对手机有什么要求？
Android 8 及以上。手机直接下载 Release 页面上的安装包即可，模拟器用的 x86_64 版在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。在手机上运行 DSH 要先准备内置的运行环境，请预留约 1 GB 空间；只连电脑或服务器上的 DSH 可以不装。

## 从源码构建 以下流程面向 **Linux x86_64**。当前工具链脚本默认安装 JDK 17、Flutter 3.47.7 和 Android SDK/NDK；App 要求 Dart `^3.13.5`。准备 Bash、Git、curl、tar、unzip、xz、Python 3、zstd（Python 未提供 `compression.zstd` 时用于解包 zstd 压缩的 deb）、file 和常见 GNU 命令；重新解析 Ubuntu 软件包锁时还需要 gpgv。 先取得完整源码和项目资源。`app/pubspec.yaml` 声明的字体、图片等都是构建输入，运行时包由下面的脚本生成。 ```bash git clone https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go.git cd dsh-go bash tooling/setup-toolchain.sh source tooling/env.sh flutter --version java -version bash runtime/build-runtime.sh arm64-v8a DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f arm64 --keep-daemon ``` 工具链脚本会下载 SDK/NDK 与模拟器镜像，并执行 Android SDK 许可接受步骤。默认安装到 `~/dev`；可通过 `DEV_ROOT` 指定独立目录。脚本会复用已有安装，构建前请核对版本。 产物为 `app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-release.apk`。运行时构建使用仓库固定的版本与校验信息，并需要联网下载依赖。示例中的 `DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE=` 不嵌入维护者的内测通道令牌；`--keep-daemon` 保留 Gradle daemon，适合同时开发其他 Android 项目的环境。 构建 x86_64 包时，先生成对应运行时： ```bash bash runtime/build-runtime.sh x86_64 DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f x64 --keep-daemon ``` 未配置 `app/android/key.properties` 时，本地 release 构建使用 debug 签名。它不能直接覆盖不同签名的官方安装包；请在测试设备上安装，保留已有数据，不要为解决签名冲突直接卸载正在使用的 App。发布签名与密钥文件不要提交到仓库。 只查看 APK 构建命令，可运行： ```bash DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh --dry-run -f all ``` ## 目录 | 路径 | 内容 | | --- | --- | | `app/` | Flutter 界面与 Android Kotlin 平台实现 | | `packages/dsh_client/` | DSH Web API 的 Dart 客户端 | | `packages/dsh_remote/` | DSH Remote 的 Dart 客户端 | | `runtime/` | Linux 运行时打包、引擎补丁与 App 桥接 | | `sdk/plugin-kit/` | 原生插件作者工具包；在仓库中使用，未发布到 npm | | `examples/plugins/` | 插件示例 | | `docs/guide/`、`docs/plugins/` | 用户指南与插件开发文档 | | `docs/assets/` | 本页用到的展示图、桌宠动图和社群二维码 | | `tooling/` | 工具链、APK 构建与诊断脚本 | | `services/`、`site/`、`infra/` | 配套分享服务、网站和部署材料 | ## 参与贡献 问题反馈和改进建议可提交到 [Issues](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/issues)。代码、文档和翻译贡献请先看 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)。插件作者可以从[插件教程](docs/plugins/README.md)和 [SDK](sdk/plugin-kit/README.md)开始。 安全问题请按 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 报告，避免在公开 Issue 中提交漏洞细节或凭据。 ## 社区 -
